designDecisions: P-248: one module, site-plan/footprint-layer.ts, owns the atom-to-composer mapping, the human labels ('Existing structure', 'ML-derived', 'unsurveyed') and the legend sentences. Every sheet reads the composed SitePlanFootprintsModel, so no surface re-derives a footprint from a raw atom.

P-248: drawn from the model's own local-ENU rings through EACH sheet's existing transform (aerial.toPage / toPage), never a second projection, and never a fill over the aerial imagery -- on that sheet the imagery IS the evidence the footprint is reconciled against.
P-248: footprints draw UNDER the property line, so the heaviest curve on the sheet stays the parcel edge.
P-248: a footprint that contradicts the appraisal record inherits the existing P-159 contradiction treatment rather than inventing a second one.

P-261: ONE predicate in ONE new module, site-plan/envelope-promotion.ts, mirroring the hauska-map predicate including its sourceCitation fallback, with the marker constant imported from depth-warm/types.ts rather than re-typed.

P-261: the marker is read at the ONE place the atom is loaded (resolveEnvelopeOutcome, author.ts) and carried to the composer as a boolean, so the composer never re-reads provenance and there is exactly one reader.
P-261: the refusal sentence is number-free by construction and a test asserts no digit appears in it.

P-261: confirmed by reading, not assumed, that every renderer that prints a figure already reads printedBuildable (P-159): render.ts:605/1510, layout.ts:935, feasibility.ts:299/811, report-model.ts:295, and the narrative guard narrative-generator.ts:255.

knownRisksRegistered: Decoded-text assertions on a PDF are only as strong as the decoding: a phrase drawn across a wrapped line arrives as several operands, and Inter's ligature glyphs come back as Unicode presentation forms (U+FB01). Both were hit for real on this lane and are handled explicitly (CP2) rather than by weakening the assertion to a word that happens to survive.

The promotion predicate is now the second implementation of the same fact in this fleet. A change to either side needs the divergence test the dispatch names; this lane's fixtures are the same answers the P-249 lane is told to use.
